title: Apple Launches Rental Program for Its Products
paragraphs: Apple has started a new program in the United States that lets customers lease, or rent, its products instead of buying them.
The program is called Apple Upgrade, and it began on July 28, 2026. Customers can use it in Apple stores, online and in the Apple Store app. Apple runs the program with the payment company Klarna.

Under the program, customers pay a monthly fee to use a device. They can lease iPhones and Apple Watches for 12 or 24 months, and Macs and iPads for 24 or 36 months. According to Apple's website, the cheapest iPhone lease costs $17.99 a month. The cheapest iPad and Apple Watch leases start at $11.99 a month, and Macs start at $24.99 a month.

When the lease ends, customers have three choices. They can return the device and get a new one, return the device and leave the program, or pay to keep it. Devices must be returned in good condition, and customers may have to pay extra if a device is damaged. AppleCare+, Apple's insurance and repair service, is not included in the monthly price.

Not all products are part of the program. Some cheaper products, such as the iPhone 16, the MacBook Neo, the basic iPad and the Apple Watch SE, are not included. The program is only for people aged 18 or older who live in the US.
Apple Upgrade replaces the iPhone Upgrade Program, which Apple had offered since 2015. That program let customers get a new iPhone after 12 monthly payments, and it started at about $42 a month.

The program comes as electronics are becoming more expensive. Recently, Apple raised the prices of some Macs and iPads because of a shortage of memory chips. Francisco Jeronimo, an analyst at the research company IDC, said that the program could make people see an iPhone or Mac more like a subscription than a big purchase.
